sections.overview: Uromys porculus is a rodent known from Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands.
sections.identification: The scarce remains include a narrow, elongated skull; the short tail may indicate a ground-dwelling animal.
sections.habitat: Lowland tropical forest is considered a possible habitat, but this has not been confirmed.
sections.diet: No reliable species-specific diet is documented in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: The species has not been confirmed in the wild since the late nineteenth-century collections.
sections.reproduction: The available historical specimens do not provide a documented account of reproduction.
sections.ecology: The taxonomic revision notes its morphological similarity to Uromys imperator, another little-known Guadalcanal rat; see that profile.
sections.conservation: Mammal Diversity Database lists it as Critically Endangered; it may already be extinct.
